12	
13	This task is a two-tier run, cheap gate first: the **scheduler** (a pure-code Action,
14	no model at all) ran this task's precondition (`task.mjs`, over the `commits` signal),
15	and only *because* it found a meaningful change did it dispatch you — a strong-model
16	subagent — via the `ready-for-agent` issue. Most weeks the gate skips and no strong
17	model ever boots; you are paid for solely on the weeks there's real work. (This is
18	the "cheap dispatcher front door" cost model — the scheduler precondition is that
19	front door, cheaper than a dispatcher session because it runs no model.)
20	
21	So **you don't re-run that gate.** The dispatch issue's **Context** names the
22	substantive commits in the window; treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate
23	whether to run. Still: **most runs correctly change nothing** (below), so "ran" never
24	means "must produce a PR".
25

27	
28	```sh
29	npm install && npm run test:live
30	```
31	
32	The gate prints a "bare generic value differences (informational)" block and a
33	per-exemplar matrix (✓ match · ~ different value · ✗ missing · — n/a): a `~` is a
34	concrete generic gap the extractor gets wrong, a `✗` a field it finds nothing for —
35	your candidate targets. This run is your pre-change reference (the committed

42	## 3. Improve — the feedback loop
43	
44	Pick one or a few `~`/`✗` gaps and close them, iterating: **hypothesize → edit only
45	the generic extractor / helpers → `npm run test:live` → compare to the baseline**,
46	until you have one or more clean wins (or conclude there are none). Every change

50	- **Generic only** (postcondition: *scope*). Key off a widely-used convention that
51	  would help unseen sites — display conventions (date↔time separators, start–end
52	  ranges, "Event @ Venue" titles, ordinals) or machine-readable signals (schema.org
53	  JSON-LD, OG/meta, microdata, `<time datetime>`). Lifting one `custom/<site>.js`'s
54	  logic or special-casing a host is out of scope: if the only beneficiary is a
55	  single case and the rule wouldn't fire elsewhere, it isn't generic. **The only
56	  files you may leave changed are `generic-extractor.js`, `helpers/*.js`, your
57	  covering test in `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, and the
58	  regenerated generic-coverage GENERATED artifacts** — anything else fails scope.

     3	# Postcondition for the create-extractor task's AGENT stage (task.md §4): validate
     4	# the agent's work before the draft PR is marked ready for review.
     5	#   Exit 0   → the extraction is valid; mark the PR ready (task.md §5).
     6	#   Non-zero → do NOT mark it ready. The agent bails: close the PR and hand the
     7	#              issue to a human, quoting the printed reason. Reverts nothing — a
     8	#              scope violation FAILS the run (the human PR review is the backstop,
     9	#              per the pipeline's containment model), rather than silently
    10	#              rewriting the agent's work.
    11	#
    12	# Takes NO env. Everything it needs is derivable from the branch preprocessing
    13	# pushed: the case name from the branch, the source from the recorded page's own
    14	# host. (It used to read five env vars the agent threaded through from a triage
    15	# JSON blob — that hand-off is gone now that preprocessing owns the names and
    16	# commits them, and derived-here can't drift from what was actually built.)
    17	
    18	set -uo pipefail
    19	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
    20	TASK_DIR=".claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/create-extractor"
    21	
    22	fail() { echo "POSTCONDITION FAILED — do not mark the PR ready, hand the issue to a human: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
    23	
    24	BRANCH="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
    25	case "$BRANCH" in
    26	  claude/extractor/*) ;;
    27	  *) fail "not on a claude/extractor/* branch (on '$BRANCH') — work on the draft PR's head branch" ;;
    28	esac
    29	CASE_NAME="${BRANCH#claude/extractor/}"
    30	CASE_FILE="dev/requirements/extractor/expected/$CASE_NAME.json"
    31	URL_FILE="dev/requirements/extractor/data/server-fetched/$CASE_NAME.url"
    32	[ -f "$CASE_FILE" ] || fail "no case at $CASE_FILE — was this branch scaffolded by the task's preprocessing?"
    33	[ -f "$URL_FILE" ]  || fail "no recorded URL at $URL_FILE — was this branch scaffolded by the task's preprocessing?"
    34	
    35	# The source that owns this case's host, asked of the sources' real matches() — the
    36	# same authority triage used, so this can't disagree with what was scaffolded.
    37	SRC_BASE="$(node "$TASK_DIR/resolve-source.js" "$(cat "$URL_FILE")" 2>/dev/null)"
    38	[ -n "$SRC_BASE" ] || fail "no source matches this case's host — the scaffold's matches() is missing or was edited"
    39	SRC="extension/event-extractors/custom/$SRC_BASE.js"
    40	
    41	# The last commit preprocessing made on this branch (the scaffold, then the page
    42	# record). `git log` is newest-first, so the first match is the baseline the agent's
    43	# work sits on top of; fall back to the newest branch-only commit.

    50	#    file) fails the run. The recorded page is INSIDE the baseline now

    52	#    re-recorded page is exactly the kind of drift this should catch.
    53	#    The one other allowed outcome is the "nothing to override" one (task.md §3):
    54	#    when the core generic extractor already covers the site, the agent DELETES

## Audit: GCEC local tasks vs. the Claudinite "precondition decides, later stages don't" rule

Pack: `gcec` (`/workspace/missingbulb/googlecalendareventcreator/.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/`). Two tasks. Most severe first.

---

### 1. `create-extractor` — VERDICT: **borderline** (2 flags), plus the pack's only 2026-08-06 breakage

| field | value |
|---|---|
| pack | `gcec` |
| agent_model | `sonnet` (`task.mjs:25`) |
| frequency | `hourly` (`task.mjs:23`) |
| prework | **yes** — `agent_preprocessing: 'node prepare.mjs'` (`task.mjs:36`) |
| CLAUDINITE_REQUEST_AGENT | **yes** — read `prepare.mjs:366`, written `prepare.mjs:501-506` |
| LEGACY field names | **YES — both** (see breakage below) |

**Hand-off gate (correct).** The agent request is written only after a page was recorded, pushed, and a draft PR opened (`prepare.mjs:486-507`). The gating condition is "a real page is recorded and an `extract()` is left to write" — work the code genuinely cannot do. It does **not** re-check whether the run should have happened. This is textbook-correct.

**Flag A — agentic-stage stop on state, `task.md:20-21`:**
> `If the issue carries no `### Delivered` section, preprocessing created nothing — comment` / `that and stop.`

The prework only requests the agent *after* delivering, so this branch means a broken prerequisite. It is written as a quiet comment-and-stop rather than a failure, which reads as a discretionary "already-handled / nothing here" skip in the agentic stage. Should be phrased as a hard failure ("the dispatch is malformed — fail the run"), not a stop.

**Flag B — worker re-derives the precondition's own predicate, `prepare.mjs:392-396`:**
```
const requests = eligible(allRequests);
if (!requests.length) {
  console.log('create-extractor: nothing eligible to act on this run');
  return;
}
```
with the intent stated explicitly at `prepare.mjs:76-77`:
> `// eligibility exactly so the gate and the worker can never disagree about what` / `// "eligible" means`

That is the worker re-litigating the gate's question. It is *mitigated* — the pending-page sweep already ran at `prepare.mjs:377` before this point, and the precondition can legitimately fire on cached-page commits with zero eligible requests (`task.mjs:81-85`), so this path is a legal empty outcome for the request half of the run. Borderline rather than a violation, but the "so the gate and the worker can never disagree" framing is the exact reasoning the rule forbids.

**Flag C (minor) — timing-based partial skip inside the worker, `prepare.mjs:316-320`:**
```
if (recorded.length + failed.length > 0 && !hasRoomToStart(Date.now() - startedAt, budgetMs)) {
  deferred.push(name);
  continue;
}
```
Work skipped for a clock reason. Defensible (SIGKILL protection, always attempts at least one, deferred items carry to the next run) but it is a timing skip in the worker stage.

**Correct by the rule (no action):**
- `prepare.mjs:435-438` — `'every eligible request was triaged closed — no agent needed'`: triage ran and closed issues; no agent needed is a *result*, not a skip.
- `prepare.mjs:302-303` `if (!pending.length) return 0;` — empty outcome.
- `prepare.mjs:469-481` — unrecordable page → `handToHuman` + `return` with exit 0. An error stop, explicitly defended at `RULES.md:169-174`. Allowed.
- `task.md:34-38` §2 bail — a judgment about the *artifact* (the page isn't one usable event), reached after doing the work, and it still delivers (closes PR, comments, relabels). Legal.

**2026-08-06 breakage — this is the real one:**
- **Legacy fields, declared and read at runtime.** `task.mjs:36-37` declares `agent_preprocessing` / `agent_preprocessing_timeout`. Worse, `prepare.mjs:377` reads the value back out of the declaration:
  `await sweepPendingPages(scraperKey, base, decl.agent_preprocessing_timeout * 1000);`
  After a rename to `prework`, the engine ignores the legacy key → **the prework subprocess never runs at all**, and if it is invoked by any other route `decl.agent_preprocessing_timeout` is `undefined` → `budgetMs` is `NaN` → `hasRoomToStart` is always false → every pending page after the first is silently deferred forever. Tests pin the legacy names too: `test/task.test.js:76,78` and `test/prepare.test.js:174-175`.
- **Scheduler-maintenance reliance.** `task.mjs:51-53` — *"The scheduler already guarantees both exist"* (the `agent-running` / `needs-human` labels), echoed at `prepare.mjs:54-58`. If label provisioning moved to the daily task-janitor, an hourly run can precede it; `addLabel` at `prepare.mjs:442` never checks its status, so a failed claim goes unnoticed and the request re-scaffolds every hour — exactly the loop the claim exists to prevent.
- **needs-human convergence.** `prepare.mjs:36` and `RULES.md:171-174` bank on *"non-zero = the task FAILED and the scheduler converges it to `needs-human`"*. That is failure-convergence, not the missing-task-file path that now closes — so it survives, but the reasoning is load-bearing and worth re-verifying after the re-vendor.
- **No `preprocess.mjs` path import.** Neither task imports it; `prepare.mjs:40-49` imports only local siblings. ---

| field | value |
|---|---|
| pack | `gcec` |
| agent_model | `opus` (`task.mjs:13`) |
| frequency | `weekly` (`task.mjs:11`) |
| prework | **no** — deliberately, with the reason recorded at `task.mjs:21-25` (no code→agent data channel for the `test:live` baseline the agent must see) |
| CLAUDINITE_REQUEST_AGENT | **no** — single agentic stage |
| LEGACY field names | **no** — `agent_preprocessing` appears only in a prose comment (`task.mjs:22`); no legacy key is declared |

This task is a positive model of the rule. The precondition is the only decider (`task.mjs:36-40`, gating on `commits.substantiveChange`), and `task.md:22-24` states the rule outright:
> `So **you don't re-run that gate.** ... treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate` / `whether to run.`

The one "stop" is a post-work empty outcome, which the rule explicitly permits:
- `task.md:87-88` — `If no clean generic win emerges, print ... and stop.` The work (baseline measure, hypothesize/edit/`test:live` loop) has already run; producing no PR is the result, not a skip. Reinforced at `task.md:23-24` (*"'ran' never means 'must produce a PR'"*) and `task.mjs:34-35`.
- `task.md:99-100` — non-zero postcondition → *"the run has FAILED. Do not retry and do not open a PR"*. An error stop; allowed.

**2026-08-06 breakage: none.** No prework, no legacy keys, no `preprocess.mjs` import, no reliance on scheduler re-arm or on needs-human convergence.

---

### Recommended fixes, in priority order
1. `task.mjs:36-37` + `prepare.mjs:377` + `test/task.test.js:76,78` + `test/prepare.test.js:174-175` — rename to `prework` / `prework_timeout` in lockstep before re-vendoring.
2. `prepare.mjs:442` — check `addLabel`'s status and fail loudly; stop assuming the scheduler pre-created the labels (`task.mjs:51-53`).
3. `task.md:20-21` — turn "comment that and stop" into an explicit run failure.
4. `prepare.mjs:76-77` — reword the comment so the eligibility re-derivation reads as "the worker acts on fresh, full issue objects", not as "the worker agrees with the gate about whether to run".
